passage: Sumit had sent the team's report without Nazia's section, and she lost marks because of it. For two days he argued, listing reasons why it was not really his fault, because admitting it felt like admitting he was nothing. Then Nazia stopped answering his messages. The silence sat like a weight on his chest. His mentor Rukmini heard him out and said, "I did much worse at your age. So what is your move?" He felt steadied, and he did not hear it as a licence to slack off; he set alarms for every future deadline. That night he stood at the mirror and said aloud, "I got this wrong, and I still deserve respect, from me too." It made the next step easier. He wrote to Nazia: "I am sorry. I sent it without your section and it cost you marks. No excuses. I will speak to the professor about a resubmission if you want. I won't push you to reply." Nazia did not answer that week. He left it, and kept his promise about the deadlines.

qa.q: Whose section did Sumit leave out of the report?
How did Sumit's first reaction to his mistake differ from what he did after talking with Rukmini?
qa.a: At first he argued with reasons why it was not his fault; after Rukmini's question and his words at the mirror, he wrote a clear apology with no excuses and offered to speak to the professor.

qa.q: What was Sumit feeling when Nazia stopped answering his messages?
qa.a: He felt guilty, with the silence sitting like a weight on his chest.

qa.q: What could Sumit do while waiting for Nazia to reply?
qa.a: He could give her space without pressing for forgiveness and keep his promise about deadlines.

grounding: After a mistake that harmed a teammate, a young man moves from defensive pride to a mentor's steadying words, self-respect and an apology that gives the other person space.
